subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which two scientists are credited with proposing the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace
Charles Darwin and Gregor Mendel
Carl Linnaeus and Carl Woese
James Watson and Francis Crick
questions.explain: Darwin and Wallace independently proposed evolution by natural selection, prompting Darwin to publish his ideas.

questions.q: In which year did Charles Darwin publish 'On the Origin of Species'?
questions.explain: Darwin set out his theory of evolution by natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859.

questions.q: The emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as MRSA provides evidence for which process?
options: Evolution by natural selection
Selective breeding
The three-domain system
Genetic engineering
questions.explain: Antibiotic resistance spreading through bacterial populations is a modern, observable example of natural selection.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly orders the Linnaean classification groups from largest to smallest?
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Phylum, Kingdom, Order, Class, Family, Species, Genus
questions.explain: Linnaeus classified organisms into a hierarchy running from Kingdom down to Species.

questions.q: In the binomial naming system, an organism's scientific name is made up of its...
options: genus and species
kingdom and phylum
family and genus
class and order
questions.explain: The binomial system names each organism using its genus followed by its species.

questions.q: The three-domain system divides living organisms into Archaea, Bacteria and...
options: Eukaryota
Protista
Fungi
Plantae
questions.explain: The three domains are Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota (organisms whose cells have a nucleus).

questions.q: Selective breeding is best described as...
options: choosing organisms with desired characteristics to breed together over many generations
inserting a gene from one organism into another
cutting DNA using restriction enzymes
cloning organisms using tissue culture
questions.explain: In selective breeding, humans choose which individuals reproduce so useful characteristics become more common over generations.

questions.q: In genetic engineering, what is the role of restriction enzymes?
options: To cut DNA at specific sequences
To join pieces of DNA together
To copy the entire genome
To transport DNA into a cell
questions.explain: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific base sequences, isolating the desired gene; ligase then joins DNA together.

questions.q: Why do fossils provide evidence for evolution?
options: They show how organisms have changed over long periods of time
They prove all species appeared at the same time
They show that organisms never change
They allow extinct species to be selectively bred
questions.explain: Fossils in rock layers of different ages reveal how organisms have gradually changed over millions of years.

questions.q: The three-domain system was developed largely because of advances in which area?
options: Analysis of genetic material such as RNA and DNA sequences
Measuring the size of organisms
Counting the number of offspring produced
Observing the colour of organisms
questions.explain: Improved analysis of genetic material, especially RNA, revealed relationships that the older systems could not show.

questions.q: Carl Woese's three-domain system differs from the earlier five-kingdom system mainly because it...
options: separates prokaryotes into Archaea and Bacteria based on molecular differences
combines all organisms into a single group
ignores genetic evidence entirely
is based only on where organisms live
questions.explain: Molecular evidence showed Archaea and Bacteria are very different, so Woese split the prokaryotes into two separate domains.

questions.q: According to natural selection, which individuals are most likely to survive and reproduce?
options: Those best adapted to their environment
The largest individuals only
Those chosen by humans
Those with the fewest mutations
questions.explain: Individuals with characteristics best suited to their environment are more likely to survive competition and reproduce.

questions.q: In natural selection, a beneficial characteristic becomes more common in a population over time because...
options: individuals with the characteristic survive and pass on the alleles for it
individuals learn the characteristic and teach it to their offspring
the environment forces every individual to change
humans breed only the individuals with that characteristic
questions.explain: Survivors reproduce and pass the useful alleles to offspring, so the characteristic increases in frequency over generations.

questions.q: A hospital finds that an infection no longer responds to a common antibiotic. Which statement best explains this?
options: Random mutations produced resistant bacteria, which survived and reproduced when the antibiotic was used
The bacteria chose to become resistant in order to survive
The antibiotic deliberately caused the bacteria to mutate
All the bacteria were resistant from the start and none died
questions.explain: Chance mutations create resistant bacteria; the antibiotic kills non-resistant ones, so resistant bacteria survive and multiply.

questions.q: During the Industrial Revolution, tree bark was darkened by soot and dark peppered moths became far more common than pale ones. The best explanation is that...
options: dark moths were better camouflaged from predators, so more survived and reproduced
the soot dyed the moths a darker colour
the moths decided to change colour to hide
pale moths flew away to cleaner areas
questions.explain: On sooty bark dark moths were harder for birds to see, so they survived and passed on their alleles more successfully.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of selective breeding is that it can...
options: reduce genetic variation, making populations more vulnerable to disease
increase the number of natural predators
instantly create entirely new species
always improve the health of the organisms
questions.explain: Repeatedly breeding closely related individuals reduces genetic variation, so a single disease can affect the whole population.

questions.q: Bacteria can be used to produce human insulin because...
options: the human insulin gene can be inserted into bacteria, which then make the protein
bacteria naturally produce human insulin without modification
bacteria are the same species as humans
insulin can only be made inside bacterial cells
questions.explain: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria, which then read it and produce human insulin.

questions.q: In genetic engineering, a plasmid is often used as a vector because it can...
options: carry a gene into a host cell
cut DNA into fragments
join DNA strands together
kill unwanted bacteria
questions.explain: A plasmid acts as a vector, carrying the desired gene into the host cell so it can be expressed.

questions.q: A farmer grows a crop that has been genetically modified to make its own insecticide, reducing losses to insect pests. This is an example of...
options: genetic engineering to improve crop yield
natural selection
selective breeding over many generations
classification
questions.explain: Inserting a gene so the crop makes an insecticide is genetic engineering, used here to increase yield.

questions.q: A farmer wants cows that produce more milk, so over many generations he breeds together only cows and bulls from high-milk-yield families. This process is...
options: selective breeding
genetic engineering
natural selection
tissue culture
questions.explain: Choosing which individuals reproduce to enhance a desired characteristic over generations is selective breeding.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Biology (1BI0) specification; Natural Selection & Genetic Modification
